A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RefAM, with matching authors, core method, benchmarks and figures. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantive experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original image and video segmentation results, attention analyses, component ablations and additional inversion experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation experiments and adds SD3.5 backbone and encoder results in Section 4.3 and Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: v2 removes the optional inversion-based feature-collection procedure described in v1 Appendix A.1. The central attention-magnet augmentation, filtering, heatmap aggregation and SAM-based segmentation procedure remains unchanged. SD3.5 is evaluated using the existing framework.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate RefCOCO/+/g, Ref-DAVIS17, Ref-YouTube-VOS, MeViS, ImageNet-Segmentation and PascalVOC single-class segmentation. The added backbone and attention-magnet configurations use existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes TAS from both metric comparisons and removes the weakly supervised CLRL and PPT comparisons from mIoU. The remaining image comparators, video comparator set and external methods in the ImageNet/Pascal comparison are retained.

E3.justification: The reported FLUX feature-extraction timestep changes from 750 to 520. v2 introduces SD3.5 at timestep 640, T5-only/CLIP-only/combined encoder configurations with and without attention magnets, and a scene-description magnet control. The inversion evaluation is removed. These substantially revise the experimental configurations without changing dataset coverage.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix A.1 add analyses testing generalization beyond FLUX and the contributions of T5 versus CLIP. v2 Table 6 adds a scene-description attention-magnet alternative, while v1's inversion-benefit analysis disappears. Representation-space, caption-conditioning, SAM2-size and video component analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The five sampled stop-word sets and '(5x)' annotations for random variants remain in v1 Table 5/v2 Table 6. Figure 4's shaded bands are unchanged. No new seed information, repeated-run reporting or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: FLUX image benchmark and component-ablation values are extensively replaced: for example, RefCOCO val mIoU changes from 57.24 to 52.17 under different reported timesteps, not a matched-setting deterioration. v2 adds SD3.5, encoder, scene-description and efficiency results and removes inversion results. Video benchmark scores and retained non-inversion ImageNet/Pascal scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Removing v1 Appendix A.1 also removes its rectified-flow inversion differential equation and associated vector-field and correction-factor definitions. The remaining mathematical formulation is retained; changing sigma to sigma_t is a notation refinement. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract changes consistent superiority to superiority on most datasets, and the introduction now claims state-of-the-art or competitive results. Section 4.1 narrows the claim to four of six datasets. The core contributions remain unchanged, and the conclusion still repeats the earlier broader superiority claim, making the qualification incomplete.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation attributing structural grounding to T5 and characterizing CLIP as insensitive to syntax. Its claim that removing stop words can improve CLIP conflicts with Tables 7–8, which show lower scores without attention magnets. The inversion accuracy–latency discussion disappears, while Appendix D's limitations and the existing GAS interpretation remain.

D1.justification: v2 reports approximately 460 ms per image and 22 GB memory for FLUX-dev on an A100 and promises public code. It removes v1's setup details covering 28 denoising steps, batch size one, 5–8 parallel expressions and inversion timings, plus the disclosure of author screening of generated captions. The code promise does not establish actual availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds Esser et al. and Yuksekgonul et al., explicitly contrasts attention magnets with Darcet's learned registers, and removes the attribution of preprocessing to HybridGL. References associated with removed baselines and inversion disappear. Numerous venue/year changes concern retained works rather than different research.

P1.justification: There are localized wording corrections and expanded explanations. Section 4.1 is retitled, Section 4.3 is added, Appendix A.1 is replaced, and the LLM-use disclosure is removed. Most existing prose and the overall organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a CLIP indicator column and top-three highlighting. New encoder tables replace the inversion table, other tables are reordered, and several figures move with the text. All fourteen figures retain their visual content, although Figure 10's caption drops the inversion attribution.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence beyond FLUX and partially corrects overbroad performance claims. However, its new encoder interpretation contradicts its own tables: CLIP TestA mIoU is 46.3 with attention magnets and 44.8 without, despite the claimed benefit from removal. The conclusion remains insufficiently qualified, and batching and caption-curation disclosures are lost. These benefits and reporting weaknesses leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
